description.description: Project is authored/hosted on Lovable; changes made via Lovable auto-commit to the repo, and local IDE pushes are reflected back.
npm run build emits dist/; the entire contents must sit at the document root so index.html is served directly.
CloudPanel runs Nginx, which never reads .htaccess, so the try_files directive in the vhost is the only working SPA fallback there.
public/.htaccess is copied into dist/ automatically; requires mod_rewrite enabled on cPanel/shared hosting.

React Router routes such as /checkout exist only in the browser; a refresh or shared deep link asks the server for a path with no file on disk, so the server returns its own 404 and the app never boots.
Any request that is not a real file must return index.html with HTTP 200; only the per-server syntax differs.
Panels split by whether they read .htaccess: CloudPanel and plain Nginx need a vhost edit, LiteSpeed/Apache ship .htaccess in dist/, Netlify uses _redirects and Vercel uses vercel.json.

For a PHP site in CloudPanel, Nginx already routes unknown paths to index.php, so a one-line index.php readfile serves the SPA without vhost access. Explicitly a workaround, not a fix: it adds a PHP round trip to every page load; prefer try_files.

Authenticates its own caller via the Razorpay payment signature HMAC rather than a Supabase JWT.
Acts as the safety net that settles an order even when the browser never returns; authenticates callers with the x-razorpay-signature HMAC.

Final backstop: GET /v1/orders/{id}/payments returns every attempt Razorpay recorded (failures included), so it can repair any order whose status disagrees with the money. Authenticates with a Bearer service role key compared in constant time, so it must never be called from the browser.
Not deployed (404), which is why GST does not show at checkout.
Browser verification, webhook and reconcile can each settle an order; all three are idempotent so it does not matter which one wins.
Records order creation at the gateway with receipt = order_<wooId>, which is how a debited-but-orderless payment is traced back.

One row per attempt, with a unique constraint on (provider, gateway_payment_id) and upsert-only writes so Razorpay duplicate deliveries and the authorized to captured progression collapse into one row.
Collapses attempts to one row per gateway order so paid-after-failure orders are visible.

SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are injected by the platform and must not be added manually (Supabase rejects SUPABASE_-prefixed secrets). Secrets only apply to functions deployed after they are set, so changing one requires a redeploy.
Self-generated (openssl rand -hex 32) and must match the Razorpay dashboard exactly; a mismatch is the number one cause of 'webhook fires but nothing happens'.

description.description: Only the public Key ID may be exposed in a VITE_ variable; the Key Secret in a VITE_ variable must be rotated immediately. VITE_ values are baked into the bundle at build time, so a new value needs a new build.

Mandatory for razorpay-webhook: Razorpay cannot send a Supabase token, so with JWT verification on every webhook is rejected with 401 before the function code runs. Each function authenticates its own callers instead.

payment.captured, payment.authorized, payment.failed and order.paid are all required; payment.failed specifically underpins the retry story by recording the failed first attempt. Razorpay retries failed deliveries up to 5 times with backoff, and webhook config does not carry over from Test to Live Mode.

The original flow silently lost paid orders: the browser PUT the order to failed on the first decline, and the webhook only promoted orders in pending/on-hold, so a successful retry was skipped. Now the browser writes failed/cancelled only in ondismiss (guarded by paymentSucceeded), and both webhook and verify promote from pending, on-hold, failed or cancelled to processing while never touching processing, completed or refunded; recovered orders carry _payment_recovered_from meta for auditing.
Cancelling restores WooCommerce stock and moving back to processing reduces it again, so recovery from cancelled logs a 'verify stock levels' warning for tight inventory.
All order state writes go through the WooCommerce REST API with consumer key/secret; orders carry _razorpay_payment_id and _payment_verified_via meta.
Uses pg_cron + pg_net to POST a sweep; the service role key is stored in Vault rather than inlined in the job definition.
Both payment tables enable RLS with zero policies, making them invisible to the anon key and readable only via the service role (SQL editor, edge functions).
Test and live keys are separate and webhook config does not carry over, so every step must be repeated in Live Mode and all four functions redeployed.

Uses Razorpay test card 4111 1111 1111 1111 and test VPAs failure@razorpay / success@razorpay; killing the tab before the success toast proves the webhook settles the order (_payment_verified_via = webhook).
